testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you NOT use the parking brake?

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if your brakes are hot from driving down a steep hill. Let them cool first, or you may damage them.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a test?
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle, the air leakage rate must not be higher than 6 psi per minute during a test.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push, the more air pressure is released to stop the vehicle.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on air brake vehicles?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air leaves the storage tanks.
The temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
The temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What should you do when parking on a flat surface?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent the vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only after applying the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent the vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, use wheel chocks. This is essential to keep the trailer from moving, especially if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: What must be on an air tank in an air-braked vehicle?
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have one-way check valves between the air compressor and the first storage tank. This stops air from leaking out.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems within about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the brake system drops below 60 psi?

options.text: Lights flash on the outside of the vehicle.
A message appears on the control panel.

questions.explanation: A low air pressure warning light will turn on if pressure drops below 60 psi. On large buses, it may turn on at 80 to 85 psi.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens once air pressure is lost and the spring brakes come on?

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks will refill automatically to a safe pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Push the correct control to release the spring brakes for a short time. This allows you to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob outward to apply the parking brakes. Push the knob inward to release them.

questions.question: What happens if one air system in a dual air brake system has very low pressure?

options.text: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
Lights on the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one air system has very low pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop your vehicle safely and have the air system repaired.

questions.question: At what air pressure level will the air compressor governor stop pumping air?
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air once the air tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What should you do when you need to make an emergency stop?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Stop while keeping your vehicle in a straight line.
Expect your vehicle to slow down faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop while keeping your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle traveling straight while still letting you turn if needed.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle, the leakage rate should be no more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, something needs to be repaired and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When a dashboard control is activated.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes come on automatically when air pressure drops too low. As soon as you see the low pressure warning, safely exit the road and bring your vehicle to a stop while you still have brake control.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: Brake fade happens when brakes are used too much and overheat, making them less effective.

questions.question: Which tool shows a driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks?
questions.explanation: A vehicle with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. It tells the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: What prevents wheel lockup when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up when brakes are applied.

questions.question: What are alcohol evaporators?

options.text: Devices that add alcohol to brake systems to prevent freezing.
Only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Devices that add alcohol to brake systems to prevent freezing.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the brake system to stop ice from forming, which can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: One air brake system with two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They use one set of controls. One system usually operates the rear brakes. The other operates the front brakes.

questions.question: When can a driver rely on front wheel braking?
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions. Front wheels rarely skid, even on ice.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, what does the ABS do?

options.text: It will improve your steering control.
It will let others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will improve your steering control.
questions.explanation: If only the tractor has ABS, it still helps you steer better. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: What can happen if you press and release the brake pedal unnecessarily?

options.text: Air escapes faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the brake system.
The brake pedal becomes more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air escapes faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too much causes air to leave the brake system faster than the compressor can refill it.
